TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng.
President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval to exercise the options to purchase 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island and 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island and execute all documents relating to these acquisitions.
Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees to exercise the options to purchase and execute all documents necessary for the acquisition of the properties located at 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island and at 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: In April 1992, the University entered into a Lease/Purchase Agreement with the University of Rhode Island Foundation (the “Foundation”) with respect to land and buildings located at 75 and 85 Briar Lane, King ston, Rhode Island (the “Briar Lane Properties”) .

The Briar Lane Properties are currently the home of URI’s Police Department and its associated surface parking lot.
In May 2000, the University entered into a Lease/Purchase Agreement with the Foundation for land and buildings located at 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island (the “Plains Road Property”).
The Plains Road Property currently houses URI’s Fire and Life Safety and Environment Health and Safety offices.
The agreements grant the University options (the “Options”) to purchase the Briar Lane Properties and the Plains Road Property (together, the “Properties”) for $1.00 each upon fulfilling the University’s lease payment obligations.
It has been determined by the University and confirmed by the Foundation that those obligations have been met.
Recommendation: After a thorough review by and with all of the appropriate stakeholders, I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the request to authorize the exercise of the Options and direct that all required action be taken to consummate the acquisition of the Properties by the University.
Supporting Information: Please see attached Exercise Notices, Lease/Purchase Agreements from 1992 and 2000.

Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees hereby approves the request to exercise the University’s options to acquire title to the properties located at 177 Plains Road and 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island, as granted to the University pursuant to the provisions of those Lease/Purchase Agreements related thereto and presented, and that the Board Chair, President and Vice President of Administration and Finance are each individually authorized, for and on behalf of the University and the Board of Trustees, to take all such actions and to execute all such documents as such person deems necessary and appropriate in furtherance of exercising such options and consummating the acquisition of the foregoing properties as recommended and presented.

February 9, 2024 The University of Rhode Island Foundation & Alumni Engagement 79 Upper College Road Kingston, Rhode Island 02881 Re: 177 Plains Road Kingston, Rhode Island 02881 Ladies and Gentlemen: Reference is made to that certain Lease/Purchase Agreement entered into on May 9, 2000 and approved by the Rhode Island State Properties Committee (the “SPC”) on May 16, 2000 (the “Agreement”) by and between the University of Rhode Island Foundation, a Rhode Island nonprofit corporation now known as The University of Rhode Island Foundation & Alumni Engagement (the “Foundation”), and the Board of Governors for Higher Education for the State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations (the “Board of Governors”) with respect to the land and buildings located at 177 Plains Road, South Kingstown, Rhode Island, currently designated by the Tax Assessor of the said Town of South Kingstown as Lot 15 on Plat 22-2 (the “Property”).

The University of Rhode Island, a public institution of higher education established by the laws of the State of Rhode Island, for itself and on behalf of its governing board, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, a public corporation created and established pursuant to Chapter 32, Title 16 of the General Laws of Rhode Island (together, the “University”), is the successor by statute to the Board of Governors and, pursuant to the provisions of Section 7 of the Agreement, possesses all rights and obligations of the Board of Governors under the Agreement, including the right to execute and deliver this notice to the Foundation and perform thereunder.

Section 5 of the Agreement grants to the University the right to purchase the Property for the sum of One ($1.00) Dollar by providing written notice to the Foundation of the University’s election to exercise the right to purchase (the “Exercise Notice”), provided, however, (a) prior to the date of the Exercise Notice, the University must have paid to the Foundation an amount in aggregate lease payments required to amortize the aggregate cost incurred by the Foundation in acquiring the Property (the “Foundation’s Acquisition Cost”) over equal to the period from the date the Foundation acquired the Property through the date of this Exercise Notice (the “Amortization Term”) at an interest rate equal to ten (10%) percent per annum (the “Agreed Interest Rate”) and (b) on and prior to the date of the Exercise Notice, the University shall have fulfilled all of its payment and other obligations under the Agreement.

The University of Rhode Island Foundation & Alumni Engagement -2- February 9, 2024 This letter constitutes the Exercise Notice.
The University represents the following to the Foundation: 1.
No event of default by the University has occurred and continues to be in effect in regard to the performance of its obligations under the Agreement; 2.
The Foundation’s Acquisition Cost was $212,000.00; 3.
Prior to the date hereof, the University has paid an amount to the Foundation in excess of the amount required to amortize the Foundation’s Acquisition Cost over the Amortization Term at the Agreed Interest Rate.
The University hereby further notifies the Foundation that the conveyance of the Property (the “Closing”) shall take place on a date to be agreed upon by the Foundation and the University following the approval of the conveyance described herein by the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees and the SPC.

At the Closing, the Foundation shall execute and deliver to the University a warranty deed in form and substance satisfactory to the University (the “Deed”) executed by a duly authorized officer of the Foundation conveying title to the Property to the University free and clear of all liens and encumbrances of record.
The University shall be responsible for the costs of recording the Deed in the Land Evidence Records of the said Town of South Kingstown.
Upon the recording of the Deed as aforesaid, the Agreement shall be deemed terminated and of no further force and effect.
Please confirm the agreement by the Foundation to the foregoing terms, including the accuracy of the representations by the University herein.
Upon receipt of a countersigned copy of this Exercise Notice, the University shall seek the required approvals of both the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees and the SPC.
